# From a fresh laptop to a local site
::: {.lead}
Install the tools, restore the recorded environment, and render the curriculum.
Initial package compilation can take considerably longer than a routine rebuild.
:::
:::

## Before you start

Install these tools before restoring the project:

- **R**, version 4.6.1 for the recorded environment — <https://cloud.r-project.org>
- **RStudio Desktop** (or Positron, optional) — <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/>
- **Quarto**, version 1.10.19 — <https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/>
- **Git** — <https://git-scm.com/downloads>
- **Python 3**, version 3.9 or newer, available as `python3`
- **Node.js**, version 24 or newer, including npm

A remote R environment such as [Posit Cloud](https://posit.cloud) may also be
used, provided it has these prerequisites and enough memory and installation
time. That hosted environment is not part of the local qualification.

A few OS-specific notes:

- On **macOS**, install the Xcode command-line tools once with
  `xcode-select --install` so R can build packages from source. Homebrew
  users also need `brew install cmake fftw pkg-config` for native dependencies.
- On **Windows**, install [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/)
  matching your R version; some packages in the `renv` lock file build from
  source on first use.
- On **Linux**, install the development headers listed by `sudo apt install`
  — most commonly `libcurl4-openssl-dev`, `libssl-dev`, `libxml2-dev`,
  `libfontconfig1-dev`, `libfreetype6-dev`, `libharfbuzz-dev`, `libfribidi-dev`,
  and `libgit2-dev`, `libfftw3-dev`, and `cmake`.

## Clone and restore

```bash
git clone https://github.com/CTTIR/courses.git
cd courses
Rscript -e 'renv::restore(prompt=FALSE)'
npm ci
Rscript setup_check.R
```

[`renv`](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/) restores the versioned package records
into the project library. Native packages may require additional system headers;
read the first installation error if restoration fails. The R version itself and
system libraries are not installed by `renv`.

`setup_check.R` is read-only. It reports missing packages, version mismatches, or
missing command-line tools and exits with a failure status until they are fixed.
It never silently installs or upgrades packages. The lockfile covers executable
lessons and the local Shiny apps; optional chunks marked `eval: false` describe
additional workflows and do not claim to have run without their data or tools.

## Render the site locally

Two commands, depending on what you want:

```bash
quarto preview    # live-reloading local server (good for writing)
quarto render --profile verify  # fresh execution and build into docs/
```

To render a single lab without touching the rest of the site:

```bash
quarto render course1_foundations/labs/lab_week1_session1.qmd
```

This will produce both the HTML article and the Reveal.js slide deck,
because each lab declares both formats in its front matter.

## Render only articles or only slides

Occasionally you want just one of the two outputs:

```bash
quarto render course1_foundations/labs/lab_week1_session1.qmd --to html
quarto render course1_foundations/labs/lab_week1_session1.qmd --to revealjs
```

The `--to` flag selects one of the formats declared in the front matter
and skips the other.

For routine prose edits, `quarto render` may reuse locally frozen calculations.
The `_freeze/` cache is not distributed with the source. Before
release, use the verification commands in the README, including the standalone
script and complete-site checks.

## Folder tour

```
courses/
├── _quarto.yml                  site configuration
├── index.qmd                    home
├── about.qmd                    philosophy and licence
├── get_started.qmd              you are here
├── schedule.qmd                 linked index of every artefact
├── references.qmd               sources and teaching ecosystems
├── css/ and assets/*.scss       site-wide look and feel
├── assets/slides.scss           Reveal.js theme
├── setup_check.R                read-only environment check
├── renv.lock                    pinned package versions
├── appendices/                  research workflow, decision tree, glossary, …
├── shared/                      data notes and site-wide images
├── course1_foundations/
│   ├── index.qmd                course landing page
│   ├── schedule.qmd             course-level linked index
│   ├── labs/                    20 .qmd labs (each renders HTML + slides)
│   └── code/                    20 matching R scripts
├── course2_regression/          …same structure
├── course3_design_causal/       …same structure
└── course4_ml_highdim/          …same structure
```

## How to read a lab

Every inference lab follows the same five steps:
**Hypothesis → Visualise → Assumptions → Conduct → Conclude.**
Workflow labs (setup, visualisation, reporting) use the variant
**Goal → Approach → Execution → Check → Report.** Once you have read
one lab the rest will feel familiar: the first section tells you what is
being asked, the second shows what the data looks like before any
modelling, the third says whether the method is appropriate, the fourth
runs it, and the fifth writes the conclusion in the form a reviewer
wants to see it.

Sections are consistent across labs:

1. **Learning objectives** — three bullets you should be able to tick off.
1. **Background** — the why and the where-this-fits.
1. **Setup** — packages and seed.
1. **1. Hypothesis** (or Goal)
1. **2. Visualise** (or Approach)
1. **3. Assumptions** (or Execution)
1. **4. Conduct** (or Check)
1. **5. Concluding statement** (or Report)
1. **Common pitfalls** — two to four bullets worth knowing by heart.
1. **Further reading** — one to three freely accessible references.
1. **Session info** — R and package versions used to build this page.

## How to present a lab

Open any file named `*_slides.html` in your browser. These are standard
[Reveal.js](https://revealjs.com) presentations:

- <kbd>F</kbd> — full-screen
- <kbd>S</kbd> — speaker-notes window (second screen)
- <kbd>O</kbd> — slide overview
- <kbd>?</kbd> — keyboard-shortcut help

If you are presenting from your own clone, `quarto preview` will hot-reload
the slides as you edit — which is a surprisingly enjoyable way to iterate
on a talk.

## Getting help

- The [Common errors](appendices/common_errors.qmd) appendix covers most
  setup and render problems.
- Open a GitHub issue for anything we have not covered; include your OS,
  your R version, your Quarto version, and the exact command you ran.
